title: 24-year-old runner Rachel Apa dies after collapsing during NYC Marathon
text:
24-year-old runner Rachel Apa dies after collapsing during NYC Marathon - ABC7 New York 
 24/7 Live New York City New Jersey Long Island Northern Suburbs Connecticut HEALTH & FITNESS 
 24-year-old runner Rachel Apa dies after collapsing during NYC Marathon 
 Pedro Rivera has details on the death of Rachel Apa. Bucknell University Tuesday, November 3, 2026 6:06PM Share Follow abc7NY on Google A 24-year-old runner died after suffering a medical incident during Sunday's New York City Marathon, according to New York Road Runners.
 The runner, Rachel Apa, was competing in her first marathon when she collapsed near Mile 24 of the race, according to reporting by The New York Times.
 Bucknell University 
 New York Road Runners said CPR was first administered by a bystander before the organization's medical staff took over, continued CPR and used an automated external defibrillator. EMS then transported Apa to Mount Sinai Medical Center, where lifesaving efforts continued before her death.
 According to The New York Times, Apa was a former Division I field hockey player at Bucknell University and was running to raise money for Parkinson's disease research in honor of her grandfather.
 Apa's cause of death was not confirmed by the NYRR. Her father told The New York Times in an interview published Monday that his daughter died of rhabdomyolysis, a life-threatening condition that can develop during physical activity .
 "It's unfathomable," Steve Apa, who could not be reached by ABC News, told the NYT of his daughter's unexpected death. "Perfect health, perfect shape, 24 years old."
 "We are deeply saddened by Rachel's passing following running in Sunday's race. Our thoughts and sincere sympathies are with her family, friends, and the entire running community," New York Road Runners said in a statement.
 According to her fundraising page for the Parkinson's Foundation Champions team, Apa was running the marathon in honor of her grandfather, who died from Parkinson's disease in 2022. In a message on the page, she wrote that her grandfather taught her to "stay active, push my limits, and embrace challenges" and said she hoped to raise money and awareness for Parkinson's research and care.
